name: Salmon River (Riggins)
blurb: Lower Salmon country. Day floats past Riggins, or the multi-day Hammer Creek to Heller Bar desert canyon.

sections.notes: Whitewater below Riggins includes Time Zone Rapid, rated Class III–IV in the BLM guide, plus other rapids whose difficulty changes with flow. Plan for experienced whitewater skills and current local guidance; jet boats may be present.

notices.title: Time Zone Rapid: Class IV potential
notices.text: BLM’s Lower Salmon guide rates Time Zone Rapid Class III–IV. This reach should not be planned as only Class II–III water. Check current flows, obstructions and local guidance before a trip.
notices.sourceName: BLM Lower Salmon River Boater Guide — map 11

sections.routeReview: Approximate river-course overview, not a rapid-running line. The mapped course is about 8.6 miles; the existing 8-mile planning estimate is retained. Confirm the actual launch, takeout and current whitewater conditions.

putInAccess.sourceName: BLM Lower Salmon boating map and guide
putInAccess.note: Approximate launch area derived from the boat-launch symbol on BLM’s April 2026 georeferenced river map and checked against imagery. The symbol spans roughly 100 metres at map scale; this is not an exact shoreline or bank-side instruction.
putInAccess.directions: Use the signed City of Riggins boat launch beside the city park. This is not Shorts Bar or Island Bar upstream. Confirm the usable ramp and parking when setting your shuttle.

takeOutAccess.sourceName: BLM Lucile boating facility and GIS inventory
takeOutAccess.note: BLM identifies this as a Riggins-trip takeout. Its facility GIS point and current river-map symbol agree on this site; the general web-page coordinate points farther downstream and was not adopted. The marker is an approximate facility area. Day use only; no camping.
takeOutAccess.directions: Use Lucile Recreation Site off Highway 95 near milepost 203.8. This is the developed parking and launch site downstream of Old Lucile; the two launches are separate.

sections.notes: A multi-day Lower Salmon and Snake River trip. BLM describes a typical four to six days from Hammer Creek to Heller Bar. Continue roughly 20 miles down the Snake after the Salmon confluence to the WDFW Heller Bar ramp below the Grande Ronde confluence. Plan the long shuttle and check permits, required equipment and current conditions.

notices.title: Slide Rapid becomes much harder at high water
notices.text: BLM rates the Lower Salmon Class II–IV and warns that Slide Rapid reaches Class V–VI at 20,000 cfs and higher; BLM does not recommend boating at those flows. A map of the endpoints is not a rapid-running guide.
notices.sourceName: BLM Lower Salmon River Boater Guide — difficulty rating

notices.title: Heller Bar is in Washington
notices.text: The takeout is the WDFW concrete ramp on the Snake below the Grande Ronde confluence, roughly 20 river miles beyond the Salmon/Snake junction. Check the required Washington vehicle access pass and arrange the shuttle before launching.

putInAccess.sourceName: BLM Lower Salmon boating map and guide
putInAccess.note: BLM documents public boating access here. The approximate area comes from the launch symbol on BLM’s April 2026 georeferenced map, checked against imagery. It is about 160 metres south of the recreation-inventory center; the latter was not used as a launch pin. No exact landing or shore connector is claimed. Camping fees and current Lower Salmon permit/equipment rules apply.
putInAccess.directions: Use the signed Hammer Creek Recreation Site boat launch west of White Bird. Follow the facility signs from the road to the ramp; the marker identifies the approximate launch area.

takeOutAccess.operator: Washington Department of Fish and Wildlife
takeOutAccess.sourceName: WDFW Facilities GIS, Boat Ramp layer (feature 244, concrete)
takeOutAccess.note: Batch 2. Coordinate is WDFW's own boat-ramp feature. Esri World Imagery (z19, checked 2026-10-25, research/raw/batch2/heller.png) puts it on the concrete ramp about 7 m from the water on the Snake River's west bank below the Grande Ronde confluence, matching the v1 instruction to pull out river-left after entering the Snake. WDFW's hand-launch feature (layer 4, 53) is ~300 m south and was not used. Legal access: WDFW Heller Bar page (https://wdfw.wa.gov/places-to-go/water-access-sites/heller-bar-395) lists it in the Chief Joseph Wildlife Area Unit, open year-round, 1 concrete ramp and 1 hand launch, camping allowed; WaterAccessSites layer (https://geodataservices.wdfw.wa.gov/arcgis/rest/services/WP_RealEstate/WaterAccessSites/FeatureServer/1) shows WDFW-managed, no closure. Pass required.
takeOutAccess.bankSourceName: USGS NHDPlus HR flowline (flow-direction digitized) + Esri World Imagery
takeOutAccess.bankNote: Facing downstream on the Snake (flow bearing ~5, north), the ramp is on the west bank, left of the NHD centreline. Confirmed on imagery.

mapAuditNote: Official public boating access, named facility identities and approximate areas checked separately from river-course geometry. Approved sections have individual reviews; dotted lines require independent full-course checks.
